answer: Sybil resistance depends on binding each agent key to a fresh, hardware-rooted attestation of an approved MRENCLAVE, with the platform identity checked against a network quota. Since MRENCLAVE identifies enclave code, not a unique chip, this binding must also prevent one platform from registering unlimited keys. Copying a VM cannot forge that evidence; creating more identities then requires access to additional attested physical silicon, not mere duplication. Names such as jetty, onyx, and pearl gain no extra weight without distinct eligible hardware.
